chunk_findings.detail: In the no-flag `pins drivers` path, `_drivers` builds the note only from `p.lines()` and then appends “write these with: …” when `not p.empty()`; it never surfaces `p.unavailable`. With `[pins].mergiraf = true`, empty `baseline_globs`, and a git older than `mergiraf_min_git` (or a missing `mergiraf` binary), `MD.plan` should return no lines to add but a non-empty `unavailable` reason. The command still returns `O.ok` saying “nothing to add: the merge drivers are already set up” (or, if `empty()` counts unavailable, “write these with: …” even though there are no lines to write), so the unavailable driver is not reported and the user is told the setup is already complete. This violates the requirement that a driver/probe that could not run is recorded unavailable and notices name the exact next step [r-tell-dont-discover].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/pin_files.py:_drivers

chunk_findings.detail: `_mergiraf_plan` writes `{g} merge=mergiraf`, but `MERGIRAF_DRIVER` uses `-l %L`, and Git’s `%L` is filled from the `linguist-language` attribute. Given `cfg.pins.mergiraf=True` and `cfg.pins.mergiraf_globs=["*.py"]`, the planned line is `*.py merge=mergiraf`; with no `linguist-language=python`, the driver is invoked without the Python language (or with `-l` receiving an empty/missing argument), so Mergiraf cannot do the Python merge. Worse, if `.gitattributes` already contains the correct `*.py merge=mergiraf linguist-language=python`, `_have(repo, "*.py merge=mergiraf")` is false and the short line is appended, overriding the correct line.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/mergedrivers.py:100

chunk_findings.detail: `apply` writes lines that `plan` did not show, violating the consent contract. For example, with `cfg.pins.baseline_globs=[]`, `cfg.pins.mergiraf=False`, `cfg.pins.after_merge="off"`, and a configured `lease.append_only_globs=["*.log"]` not yet present in `.gitattributes`, `plan().lines()` shows no attrs/config/regenerate lines, but `apply` calls `SF.sync_attributes(repo)` and `PM.install(repo, cfg)` and can add append-only union and pins driver lines anyway.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/mergedrivers.py:136

chunk_findings.detail: `check_baselines` lists tracked paths from the index but reads the working tree. If a baseline file’s staged blob contains conflict markers or unsorted/duplicate entries while the working-tree copy has been resolved/sorted but not staged, line 150 reads the clean working tree, the function returns no failure, and a commit-time ratchet check passes the bad staged content. The check must inspect the staged blob being committed, not the working tree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/mergedrivers.py:150

chunk_findings.detail: `tracked = G.git_paths(repo, "ls-files") or []` hides a failed `git ls-files`. If `G.git_paths` returns `None`/empty because git cannot run (for example a bad repository, missing git, or locked index), `check_baselines` iterates over an empty list and returns `[]`, i.e. “no problems,” instead of recording the check as unavailable and failing open as required.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/mergedrivers.py:144

chunk_findings.detail: `_min_git` trusts `cfg.pins.mergiraf_min_git` with no hard floor at 2.44. Given `cfg.pins.mergiraf=True`, `cfg.pins.mergiraf_min_git="2.40"`, git 2.40, and a present `mergiraf` binary, `_min_git` returns `(2,40)`, `_mergiraf_plan` treats the environment as available, and `apply` writes a driver containing `%P`. Git 2.40 does not support `%P`, so the merge driver fails despite the stated “git 2.44 or later” requirement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/mergedrivers.py:72

chunk_findings.detail: Notices from `check_baselines` name only the CLI next call. For a tracked baseline file containing `b\na\n`, the function returns a message ending only in `ddflow pins drivers --check`; the conformance requirement says every refusal/notice must name the exact next call in both CLI and MCP form.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/mergedrivers.py:158

chunk_findings.detail: The docs claim that the probe (`git merge-tree`) “sees the same result as the real merge,” but for pins/golden snapshot indexes the documented driver is `merge=pinsregen` (“keep ours, regenerate after the merge”) and setup “reuses the pin driver and post-merge hook.” `git merge-tree` is a plumbing merge and does not run post-merge hooks. Given a branch where the pins file is stale relative to merged source and another branch changes source inputs, `git merge-tree` would return the kept-ours pins file, while the real `git merge` would return the regenerated pins file after the post-merge hook. That contradicts the stated probe parity for the pins/golden rows.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/merge-drivers.md:4

chunk_findings.detail: The `_git` helper calls `subprocess.run(["git", ...])` directly, and the `repo` fixture uses it for `init`, `config`, `add`, `commit`, `checkout`, and `merge`. This bypasses the project’s `infra.git` adapter and violates [r-adapters], which requires external dependencies such as git to go through a port and says tests should use a fake instead of subprocess. In an environment where `infra.git` is swapped for a fake or subprocess git is blocked, these tests either fail or exercise the wrong code path, so they do not validate the production git port.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_merge_drivers.py:15

chunk_findings.detail: When `_drivers` is called with both `check=True` and `install=True` (for example `pins drivers --check --install`), the `if check:` branch returns immediately after the baseline check and never calls `MD.apply`. The requested install is silently skipped, even though the function accepts both flags and the docstring does not mark them as mutually exclusive. This should either reject the combination or run the install after the check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/pin_files.py:_drivers

chunk_findings.detail: The no-flag `pins drivers` branch never reads `MD.Plan.unavailable`. If Mergiraf is enabled but its binary is missing (or git is older than `mergiraf_min_git`) and the plan has no writable lines, `p.lines()` can be empty, so the note becomes `"nothing to add: the merge drivers are already set up"`. The unavailable probe is hidden, violating the intent that unavailable probes are recorded and is inconsistent with the install branch, which explicitly emits `p.unavailable` as gaps.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/pin_files.py:_drivers

chunk_findings.detail: The document claims the probe using `git merge-tree` “sees the same result as the real merge” because merge-tree honours `.gitattributes` drivers. But the same document’s setup reuses a post-merge hook for pins/golden snapshot indexes (line 19: “post-merge hook of `pins regenerate --install`”). `git merge-tree` does not run post-merge hooks. For a merge where a pin change requires regenerating a golden index, the real merge runs that hook and changes the file, while the probe sees only the pre-hook driver output (“keep ours”), so the probe result differs from the actual real-merge result. This invalidates the probe’s conflict prediction and can let an unsafe merge be reported as clean.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/merge-drivers.md:4

chunk_findings.detail: `_git` invokes the real `git` binary via `subprocess.run(["git", ...])`. This violates [r-adapters], which requires external dependencies such as git to go through a `ddflow/adapters` port and tests to use a fake rather than a subprocess. The suite now depends on a system `git` in PATH and on global git configuration, so it can fail before exercising the merge-driver behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_merge_drivers.py:15

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture does not disable `commit.gpgsign`, so on any developer or CI machine with global git config `commit.gpgsign=true` (and no available signing key), the first `git commit` raises `CalledProcessError`. This makes all tests using the fixture fail before the actual merge-driver logic runs.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_merge_drivers.py:30

chunk_findings.detail: `apply` calls `PM.install(repo, cfg)` and `SF.sync_attributes(repo)` which write to `.gitattributes` and git config, but `p = plan(repo, cfg)` may evaluate `plan.unavailable` due to a missing binary or git version without raising an exception. Consequently, when `--install` is supplied while a dependency such as `mergiraf` is missing (`p.unavailable` is non-empty), `apply()` still proceeds to install whatever parts of the plan are populated (or execute sub-installs), violating the intent that a missing binary or old git reports unavailable and does not silently install partial configurations.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/mergedrivers.py:126

chunk_findings.detail: `_git` executes `subprocess.run(["git", ...], check=True, ...)` directly in the test helper without routing git calls through `infra.git` (or the repository's git infrastructure port/adapter), which violates project rule `[r-adapters]` ("Every external dependency goes through a port in ddflow/adapters: one implementation per function... git is reached only through infra.git").
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_merge_drivers.py:16
